topic: Testing and validation in iterative development

components.title: Log parsing and query techniques
components.teaches: Students practice using grep, jq, and awk to filter a 2000-line trace for specific event types, extract timestamps, and count occurrences of error codes. They learn to build reusable one‑liners for rapid evidence gathering.

components.title: Systematic trace analysis workflow
components.teaches: A step‑by‑step method is introduced: (1) segment the trace by iteration, (2) hypothesize failure categories, (3) search for signature patterns, (4) collect supporting lines, (5) validate each hypothesis against the code context. Students apply the workflow to a short trace.

components.title: Worked example: multi-failure trace analysis
components.teaches: The instructor analyses a full 2000-line trace containing three distinct failures: a permission error, a version mismatch, and a logic loop. For each failure, the exact log lines are highlighted and linked to the underlying cause.

components.title: Activity: pair analysis of new trace
components.teaches: In pairs, students receive a fresh 1500-line trace and must identify at least three failure causes, citing line numbers and error codes. They prepare a brief report and present findings to the class for peer review.

components.title: Comparison of analysis strategies
components.teaches: Students compare manual trace inspection, scripted querying, and LLM‑assisted summarisation. They evaluate speed, accuracy, and false‑positive rates on the same trace, discussing when each approach is preferable.

components.title: Discussion: validation and reporting findings
components.teaches: The class discusses how to validate identified causes (re‑run, unit test, stakeholder confirmation) and how to structure a concise failure report for developers. Emphasis is placed on actionable recommendations and traceability back to log evidence.
